content.comment_body: Hello everyone! I have a [company_name] [product_name] and want to keep the display backlight on constantly for better visibility in a dark room. Can anyone suggest how to enable the backlight on the [product_name] display? Thanks in advance. [user_name]
Hello, The backlight time on [product_name] displays cannot be configured; it's fixed by default. Maybe future versions of this equipment will address this. Best regards.
Please update: I was informed that [product_name] with [article_no] may have a controllable backlight.
Hi [user_name], Have you checked the following link: [url]? Unfortunately, it seems even with [version_no], adjustable backlight is not possible. Best regards,

Dear friend, I experienced the same backlight issue with the [company_name] [product_name]. After much effort, I found a solution: I soldered two wires into the device that, when activated, turn the light on. These wires are connected to the output Q4, and I programmed it so the backlight switches on when an input is triggered. However, this uses output Q4 so it can't be used for general purposes, and the light turns on automatically. For [company_name], as we use [product_name] daily and backlight control is important for us, it would be beneficial if this became configurable by software in future releases. Thanks. Best regards,
Hi [user_name], You might want to submit your suggestion through a support request or contact the product manager for [product_name] at your local [company_name] office.

Dear friend, To clarify, I don't see why my solution couldn't be sent to my local [company_name] distributor. If you'd like, I can explain how to control the [product_name] backlight: inside, you can connect two pins to switch on the backlight for a few seconds. By linking these wires to output Q4 and controlling them via programming, you can toggle the light on/off. I'll prepare a PDF with more photos and details. Please let me know how to contact my local [company_name] office to inform them of this solution.

Hi, Use this link to access the contact webpage: [url]. Select your country and city to view relevant fax and phone numbers. There, you can ask for the product manager for [product_name] and discuss your suggestions. At least, this is possible in my country.
The [product_name] display backlight can be activated using flag 25. You can also control it via buttons or signals.
Hello everyone, In my program I use M25 to activate the display backlight for each message. It works, but afterwards, when I press buttons on the device, nothing appears on the display.

When a backlight flag is used in programming, pressing a button will not activate the backlight. This behavior has been criticized for a while, but [company_name] has not responded to customer requests.

Unfortunately, I wanted to share my solution for the [product_name] backlight option, but as far as I can tell, versions [article_no] don't support M25 for the backlight. This method only works for [product_name] devices from [article_no] and newer. When you activate an input or cursor key, the backlight turns on for 10 seconds, with each new activation resetting the timer. Alternatively, you could assign one input or key for turning on the backlight as needed. For older hardware before [article_no], upgrading to a newer model is recommended if constant backlight is needed.

analysis.insight_summary: Users repeatedly express frustration about not being able to configure the backlight settings on [product_name] displays, especially for keeping it on in dim environments. Several users resorted to hardware modifications or programming workarounds, but these often lead to limitations such as disabling certain outputs or causing unexpected issues. There's a clear demand for straightforward software control over the display backlight, but official support for this feature varies depending on the product version, causing confusion and disappointment among users.
analysis.user_expectations: Users want reliable and configurable control of the [product_name] display backlight via software or easy configuration, ideally allowing the backlight to stay on permanently.
